product: Serupa (serupa-ds) React components, CSS and tokens

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.remarks: Icons inside controls are hidden from screen readers and the control carries the name: IconButton needs a `label`, Image needs `alt` (empty for decoration), Avatar is named by `name`. Chart is named by its `title` or an `aria-label`, describes itself in a summary and names every point by its series, category and value; Sparkline and QRCode take a required name and are `role="img"`; Illustration and IconTile are decorative unless given a `label`; Logo takes `alt`. The app writes the alternative text.

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: No component plays audio or video. Media the app adds needs its own alternative.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: No component plays video. Video the app adds needs captions.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: No component plays video.

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.remarks: No component plays live media.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.remarks: No component plays video.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.remarks: Components render native elements or the ARIA role their pattern needs; Field ties a control to its label, hint and error; Table and DataGrid mark headers with `scope` and the grid roles; DescriptionList is a `<dl>`. The roles, names and structure of every story are compared with `tools/test/baseline-aria/` on each change.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.remarks: The reading order is the order on screen, and layouts use logical properties, so right-to-left pages read and mirror in order.

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.remarks: The components' own words never point by shape, color, position or sound alone; `tools/test/voice.mjs` checks every built-in label.

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.remarks: Nothing is locked to portrait or landscape.

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.remarks: Input and the fields built on it pass `autoComplete` to the native field, and PhoneInput sets `tel`, so autofill brings the saved number with its country code. The app sets the purpose of each field about the user; the Checkout, SignUp and Profile patterns show it, and Checkout's test checks every field about the person has its token.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.remarks: States are shown by more than color: check marks, icons, bars, underlines and words, and in forced colors every selected, checked, pressed or current part still looks different from one that isn't (`src/internal/forcedColorStates.test.tsx`, every story). Chart gives each series its own marker shape or bar pattern, in the legend too. The app's own content (status dots, links in text) needs a second cue too.

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.remarks: No component plays sound.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: Text and placeholder colors meet 4.5:1 in every theme: the foundation check measures every pair in all 34 themes, brand text on its tint and on the status tints included, and axe runs on every story in the six themes with pictures and with more contrast on each change. For 17.0.0 axe also ran on every story added since 12.0.0 in all 34 themes; it found brand text on a tint at 4.3:1 to 4.4:1 in the Red, Fuchsia and Rose light themes, fixed by moving their `primary` to the 700 shade.

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.remarks: Sizes are in `rem`; every story is checked with text at 200% for clipped or hidden text.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.remarks: No component draws text as an image.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.remarks: Every story is checked at 320 CSS pixels wide for sideways scrolling; tables, grids and code scroll inside their own box.

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.remarks: Focus rings, icons that carry meaning and the edges of controls such as Slider, Switch, Meter and Progress meet 3:1 in every theme, checked with the text pairs, and so does the 2px bar that marks the keyboard-highlighted item of a menu or list box (highlight-indicator). Resting borders on text fields, Checkbox, Radio and SegmentedControl are soft by design (about 1.48:1 in light and 1.43:1 in dark), and outline buttons use the same soft line as other borders: the label, hover border and focus ring mark the control, and more contrast (data-contrast="more" or the system setting) brings back 3:1 borders. An app that must conform without that setting sets --field-border to var(--border-control).

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.remarks: Every story is checked with WCAG's line, paragraph, letter and word spacing for text cut off by its box.

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.remarks: Tooltip and HoverCard close with Escape, stay while the pointer moves onto them, and stay until the pointer or focus leaves; HoverCard's tests also cancel an open with Escape during its delay. ContextualHelp opens on a press, not on hover.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.remarks: Every component works from the keyboard, as its ARIA Authoring Practices pattern expects; each guide has a Keyboard table (`tools/test/keyboard-tables.mjs` checks every one has its keys) and the tests drive it. Anything that can be dragged has a keyboard and click alternative: Kanban's "Move to…", EventCalendar's Shift and the arrow keys, DataGrid's cell keys, TransferList's buttons.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.remarks: Focus leaves every component with Tab. Dialog, Drawer, Lightbox, CommandPalette and Tour keep focus inside while open, as a modal must, and close with Escape.

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.remarks: KeyboardShortcuts opens its help dialog on "?" by default, and useShortcut can set up other single character keys. The help dialog has a "Single-key shortcuts" switch that turns all of them off, kept for every page; shortcuts with a modifier and named keys such as F2 keep working. CommandPalette opens with Ctrl or Command and K. No other component reacts to a single character key on the page: type-ahead in menus, lists and trees, and MentionInput's "@", work only while focus is inside them.

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.remarks: A toast's time stops while it's hovered or focused and while the window is in the background, and `autoDismiss: false` keeps one until it's closed. Session time-outs are the app's; the Session time-out pattern shows one that warns two minutes ahead, keeps the session while someone types, extends it from the warning, and keeps the draft when it ends anyway.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.remarks: Only what shows that work is under way or input is awaited moves on its own: Loader, an indeterminate Progress (bar or circle), a loading Switch's spinner, Image's sweep while it loads and PinInput's blinking caret, plus a Badge with `ping`. None has a pause control of its own, and each stops when the wait ends. Under reduced motion Image's sweep and PinInput's caret stop, Progress stands still, and Loader and Switch's spinner stand still or slowly breathe. RelativeTime updates its text by itself every 15 seconds and doesn't announce it. Keep `ping` for live states only. Countdown shows the time left changing each second, with no pause of its own; it's information that keeps changing while it shows, so the app shows one only where the deadline is the point (an offer or a session), or passes `seconds` to change it less often.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.remarks: Nothing flashes: no component blinks or flashes, and the only repeating motion (Loader, a Badge's ping) is a slow fade or turn.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.remarks: SkipLink gives a "Skip to content" link, and Navbar, Sidebar, BottomNav and TabNav render navigation landmarks; AppShell lays out the header, navigation and `main`. The app places the skip link and the `main` landmark; the patterns show it, with one `main`, one h1 and the skip link first, as their tests check.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.remarks: The app titles each page.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.remarks: Focus moves in reading order; Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Lightbox, CommandPalette and Tour move focus in when they open and back to their trigger when they close.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.remarks: Link announces when it opens a new tab. The app writes link text that says where it goes.

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.remarks: Finding pages (navigation, search, a site map) is the app's.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.remarks: Heading, Field and the components' own words give headings and labels; the app writes ones that describe its content.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.remarks: Focusable controls show a 2px focus ring at 3:1 against page and field surfaces, with an outline that stays in forced colors. Menu and list box items mark the active option with the highlight fill and a 2px bar at its start, 3:1 on the fill and on the list in every theme (highlight-indicator), outlined in forced colors.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: A sticky Table, DataGrid or EventCalendar header keeps the focused row, cell or event in view below it (tested). While BottomNav, a bottom Toaster, OfflineBanner or a Fab shows, the page gets scroll padding at that edge, so focus scrolls clear of them. The app's own sticky headers need `scroll-padding-top`.

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.remarks: Swiping a Carousel also works with its buttons and dots; SignaturePad, the one component that takes a drawn path, has a Type tab to sign by typing the name instead. No component needs a multipoint gesture.

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.remarks: Buttons and controls act on release, as native buttons do; a press can be cancelled by moving off.

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.remarks: A control's accessible name starts with its visible label.

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.remarks: No component reacts to moving the device.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.remarks: Everything that can be dragged also works without dragging, by a press, a tap or the keys: Slider, Splitter, SortableList, Carousel, FileUpload, Kanban, EventCalendar, ImageCropper, SignaturePad, Table's column resize and the rest. `tools/test/drag-alternatives.mjs` finds every part that listens for a drag and names the test that shows its alternative.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: Buttons and most controls (including fields at size `sm`, 24px tall) are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels. Some are drawn smaller and pass by the spacing exception, with nothing else within 24px of their centres: SegmentedControl's `sm` segments (18px drawn, a 24px press area), Slider's thumb (16px) and Splitter's handle (8px wide). Rating's stars are 24px apart at every size, each taking presses over the whole step to its neighbours, and with `allowHalf` a star is still one target: where the press lands picks the half. A checkbox, radio or switch without a visible label needs space around it, as the spacing exception allows. Every story is measured for it (`src/internal/targetSize.test.tsx`).

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.remarks: The app sets `<html lang>`. The components' words follow the locale it gives SerupaProvider.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.remarks: The app marks text in another language with `lang`.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.remarks: Focusing a component never changes the page or opens something on its own.

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.remarks: Changing a value never navigates or submits; the app decides what happens after.

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.remarks: Navigation across pages is the app's.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.remarks: The components use the same words for the same things everywhere (one set of labels per language).

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.remarks: Where help is on each page is the app's.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.remarks: Field shows the error in words with an icon and links it to the control, which is marked invalid; ErrorSummary lists every problem and links to each field.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.remarks: Field gives every control a visible label and an optional hint, and marks required or optional ones.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.remarks: A failed native check shows a message that says what is expected (a minimum length, a format, a range): the browser's own, or the words of the locale's language pack. The app's own messages need to say how to fix the value too.

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.remarks: Dialog confirmations, TypeToConfirm and toasts with Undo give the ways to check, confirm or reverse; the app uses them where it takes money, legal steps or data.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.remarks: What a flow asks for again is the app's.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.remarks: PasswordInput never blocks paste and can show the password; PinInput takes a paste or a phone's one-time-code suggestion into every box.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.remarks: Every control has a name, a role and states kept in step (`aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, `aria-checked`, `aria-invalid`…), checked by the component tests, the ARIA baselines and a name check over every story (`src/internal/nameCheck.test.tsx`).

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.remarks: Loading, saving, toasts, counts and result changes are announced through live regions, which work inside an open Dialog too. OfflineBanner says when the connection drops and comes back, Countdown says the time left at a few steps (not every second), and TransferList, TagGroup, FieldList and Kanban say what moved or was removed.
